objectives: Hear the final /ŋ/ sound in taught words such as ring, sing, song and long.
Recognise ng as a two-letter grapheme representing one phoneme in the taught examples.
Distinguish final /ŋ/ from /n/ in listening contrasts such as sing/sin.
Avoid adding a separate /g/ sound after /ŋ/ in taught words.
concepts: A digraph uses two letters to represent one phoneme.
In taught words, ng represents the nasal phoneme /ŋ/.
The sound is made with the back of the tongue raised toward the soft palate.
Some words have additional sounds around ng; this cycle focuses on final ng in controlled words.

definitions.definition: Two letters working together to represent one phoneme.
The smallest sound unit that can distinguish words.
A sound made with air flowing through the nose.
